call_points.text: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 18-20% reiterated despite the Q1 miss.
EBITDA margin guidance of 21-24% held; Q1 came in at 23.5%.
Orders from one US space customer exceed ₹1,000 Cr, delivered by end of FY28.
Kandla plant targeted to start operations by December-end or mid-January; civil work and long-lead machines ordered.
Savli cryo and keg shops are in full production; keg utilisation guided from 30% to 50-60% by year-end.
Total fund availability of ₹331 Cr as of 30 June 2026 supports Kandla and other growth plans.
US market entry blocked until 2028 by a non-compete agreement; groundwork started.
LNG and Cryo-Scientific orders delayed by customer and regulatory approvals; management expects conversion in one or two quarters.
Container freight to Europe rose from $3,000-4,000 to $8,000-9,000, prompting customers to defer deliveries.
Transformer tank business may be discontinued as carbon steel fabrication does not fit manufacturing capabilities.
Order inflow guided at ₹450-500 Cr per quarter through FY27.
Aerospace order of about ₹200 Cr from a US private space company in Q4; more of similar size expected in Q1/Q2 FY27.
Keg capacity is 300,000 a year, running at about one-third; the building can go to 1 million kegs.
Total fund availability was ₹257 Cr at 31 March 2026, to fund Kandla and project execution.
Highview Power's next project could be 8-10x the present order value, but the first plant must be commissioned first.
Analyst pressed on three years of falling operating cash flow; CFO attributed it to contract assets, and the discussion was deferred offline.
R&D spend as a percentage of turnover was not answered; management asked for more time.

guidance.statement: Management targets 18-20% revenue growth in FY27
Order booking expected at ₹450-500 Cr every quarter
At least ₹1,200 Cr of the ₹1,514 Cr order book to be executed in FY27
FY27 revenue growth guidance of 18-20% reiterated
Order intake guidance of ₹450-500 Cr, may be revised slightly upward
Keg utilisation to rise from 30% to 50-60% by end of the year
Industrial gas (non-aerospace) segment growth of around 15-18%

industry: Industrials > Capital Goods > Industrial Products > Other Industrial Products

operating_notes.text: LNG products hold an estimated 60-65% share of the Indian market and 6-8% globally; the LNG segment was about ₹459 Cr in FY26, roughly 60% export.
Keg dispatch rose 31% to 61,000 units in FY26 but keg revenue fell to ₹26.13 Cr from ₹27.15 Cr on a smaller-keg mix; disposable cylinder revenue was around ₹150 Cr versus ₹135 Cr.
The Bahamas Mini LNG terminal order totalled about ₹240 Cr, of which about ₹160 Cr was supplied in FY26 with the balance due in FY27.
Order book of ₹1,686 Cr as of 30 June 2026 includes over ₹1,140 Cr of export orders and around ₹400 Cr from aerospace.
Orders from one US space customer exceed ₹1,000 Cr, with delivery by end of FY28 on a percentage-completion basis this year and dispatch next year.
Keg capacity is 300,000 units; utilisation was 30% and is guided to 50-60% by year-end.
